failures.criterion: 3 — same-agent rule under postgres, root path (spec acceptance 3 last paragraph; Errors row 'the recorded session row is gone')
failures.evidence: /process/started (packages/daemon/src/daemon/api/routes/process.ts:7-69) never compares rootSessionId with the tree's recorded architect session: spawnTree mints `mintBootToken(tree.root, generation)` (processes.ts:3230) — the ProcessManagerDeps.mintBootToken signature has no expected-session parameter for roots (processes.ts:153) — and the route overwrites `state.roles[<architect>].sessionId = rootSessionId` (process.ts:47-52). No api.test.ts or processes.test.ts case covers a root session mismatch (grep of both files). Under pvc the init container's LEGION_RESUME_SESSION_FILE stat (tmux: the daemon's own stat, processes.test.ts `fails a resurrection loudly when the recorded OMP session file is missing, never starting fresh`) detects a missing session before registration; under postgres that stat is skipped by design (runtime-kubernetes.ts:266), so a root pod whose row is gone boots as a fresh agent under the old tree with no signal. Architect (2026-09-15) confirmed this as a known FAIL for the implementer's corrective round: mint the root boot token with the tree's recorded architect session on resurrection; /process/started refuses a mismatch with the same 409 `Worker respawn must resume the same agent session`; one API test. Also docs/kubernetes.md:372 ('--resume=<row path> still reaches OMP, which opens the row') is silent on a missing row.
failures.severity: correctness — acceptance 3's same-agent guarantee is absent for roots under postgres

failures.criterion: 3 — same-agent rule under postgres, worker path: the spec's chain 'the daemon refuses its registration … the pod exits' (the 'pod exits' link)
failures.evidence: The worker same-agent refusal is 409 `Worker respawn must resume the same agent session` (api/routes/workers.ts:239-241 in-memory; :242-248 persisted after a restart), not LEGION-95's 403 — a relaunch is generation+1, so the 403 (workers.ts:232-235, :288-291, a second session at the same generation) never fires. The extension's exit path in bootstrapWorker (packages/pi-envoy/extensions/legion.ts:685-693) is 403-only: `if (error instanceof LegionDaemonApiError && error.status === 403) { console.error('[legion] worker boot token rejected; exiting for the daemon to respawn: …'); exitProcess(1); } throw error;` — a 409 is rethrown out of bootstrapWorker into the session_start handler (legion.ts:769) uncaught. Throwaway probe (a copy of legion.test.ts's `exits the process when the daemon rejects a stale boot token at worker/started` with the /worker/started stub answering 409 with that message; probe file deleted, nothing committed): `exits` stayed [] and the handler rejected with `POST /legion/v1/worker/started failed with 409: {"error":"Worker respawn must resume the same agent session"}`. Whether OMP exits on a rejected session_start hook was not run (no rig, by order); if it does not, the pod stays Running, the boot watchdog re-arms on a live pod, and the role never retires — not the loud, bounded chain the spec records. Not store-specific (a tmux relaunch takes the same 409), but under postgres this 409 is the only same-agent guard left for workers. Suggested for the corrective round: handle a 409 at /worker/started like the 403 in bootstrapWorker (exit) plus one extension test; the spec's mechanism sentence should name the 409 expected-session check rather than LEGION-95's 403.
failures.severity: correctness of the recorded failure chain; source-read plus an extension-level probe, OMP's hook behaviour not exercised
